maria: heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak that promotes fused kernels we see a regression when fused RoPE + FlashPaged are selected together. microbench + flamegraphs below. :eyes:

jin: ugh, can you paste the numbers? which models/seq-lens/batch shapes?
maria: quick paste (all on A100-40GB, seq=2048, batch shapes mixed: [1x2048, 8x256], rotary dim=64):
```
benchmark: flash_paged_fused_rope  tokens/sec=22.1k  p50=9.8ms  p99=58ms  gpu_util=63%
benchmark: flash_paged_no_rope     tokens/sec=27.8k  p50=7.2ms  p99=34ms  gpu_util=78%
benchmark: flash_classic_fused_rope tokens/sec=26.9k  p50=7.5ms  p99=36ms  gpu_util=76%
```

alex: interesting — seems fused_rope+flash_paged is slower than either removing rope fusion or switching to classic flash. may be memory layout / strided KV access causing more L2 thrash. i saw increased L2 read/write ratio in perf counters.

jin: do we reproduce with uniform batches? maybe the batcher mixing long and short sequences triggers odd kernel paths.
maria: repros even with uniform 8x256, but magnitude drops (24.5k vs 27.8k).
alex: stack from nsight showed extra memcpy in fused_rope path right after kv-load. pictured as a ~120us spike per layer for seq>1024.
sam: could be the fused-rope shim doing per-dim scaling with a loop that doesn't vectorize for rotary_dim % 64 != 0. what's the rotary dim here? 64, but we have an internal branch for rotated dims scaling variants (we recently added rotary-dim-scale factor).

maria: rotary dim=64 and we enabled rotary_scale=0.125 (per-model config).
jin: is the fused implementation expecting contiguous KV for flash_paged? paged layout fragments the KV pages -> extra gather. Also batching heuristic: the selector picks flash_paged_fused_rope for mixed shapes because it optimizes for tail lat, but that may be wrong here.

maria: pasted a minimal reproducer + perflog:
```bash
./bench_attention --kernel=flash_paged_fused_rope --seq=2048 --batch=1 --rotary-dim=64 --rotary-scale=0.125
# output snippet
lat_p50=9.9ms lat_p99=58.3ms tokens/s=22.0k
nsight: memcpy memcpy kernel_idx=42 time=0.12ms per-layer
```

alex: workaround: fallback kernel selector policy: prefer non-fused-rope for flash_paged when seq>1024 OR when rotary_scale != 1.0. simple, low-risk.
sam: other option: add a small padding path in fused-rope that forces vectorized loop (pad rotary dims to 128) — might fix perf without losing fusion benefits. but padding increases memory and bookkeeping.

jin: let's be empirical. action plan: 1) add a microbench CI that runs flash_paged_fused_rope vs flash_paged_no_rope across seq=[256,1024,2048], batch=[1,8], rotary_scale=[1.0,0.125] (owner: jin). 2) Add selector rule to prefer non-fused-rope for seq>1024 until we confirm fix (owner: alex). 3) Investigate vectorization/padding in fused shim (owner: sam).

perf-bot: CI job 87234 failed: attention-regressions/flash_paged_fused_rope — linking logs: https://ci.redwood/87234 (regression delta: -21% tokens/s).

maria: i'll open a perf ticket with nsight traces + reproducer. adding labels: perf, attention, fused-rope, flash_paged.

jin: thanks. i'll queue the microbench overnight and share results in this thread tomorrow. :thumbsup:
